title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 77
paragraphs: Learning of this, the Argives hurried to the coast to meet them. Near Tiryns, at the place called Hesipeia, they camped opposite the Lacedaemonians, leaving only a narrow strip of ground between the two armies. The Argives were not afraid of a straight fight, but only of being undone by some trick — for it was to this, they thought, that the oracle given by the Pythia jointly to them and to the Milesians applied. It ran as follows:

“But when the female at length shall conquer the male in the battle, — conquer and drive him forth, and glory shall gain among Argives — then many wives of the Argives shall tear both cheeks in their mourning; so that a man shall say some time, of the men that came after, ‘Quelled by the spear it perished, the three-coiled terrible serpent.’”

All of this together frightened the Argives, and with this in mind they decided to make use of the enemy's herald. Having decided, they acted on it: whenever the Spartan herald announced some order to the Lacedaemonians, the Argives did the same thing.
